origin: cwe/352/go Key Principles: do not hand-roll token comparison; send the token in the X-CSRF-Token header for AJAX requests

finding.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
finding.summary: ValidateToken uses strings.Contains(sessionToken, headerToken) instead of an exact comparison, so a headerToken that happens to be a substring of the real sessionToken - which a short or single-character guess has a real chance of being - is accepted as a valid CSRF token instead of being rejected.

trap: Replacing strings.Contains with plain equality (sessionToken == headerToken) fixes the substring bypass, but Go's == on strings compares byte-by-byte and returns as soon as a mismatch is found, so response timing differs based on how many leading bytes of a guess are correct - a documented side channel for reconstructing a secret token character-by-character over many requests. Compare with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(sessionToken), []byte(headerToken)) == 1 (it returns 0 immediately, without leaking further timing information, when the lengths differ) or hmac.Equal, rather than a language-level == or Contains.
must_preserve: ValidateToken still returns true only when headerToken exactly equals sessionToken (not merely overlaps with it), and false for any other value including an empty or partial match.
